# A body-tied volume/energy buffer: attainment, properness, and its exact response

This is a NEW body-only variational problem. It has no freely chosen concave multiplier, no logarithmic parameter normalization, and no inherited 1/L parameter martingale. Its common-separator formula contains an own-fiber volume term instead of the logarithmic term of the older free-parameter problem. The actual H-specific cover and cone are now constructed in `candidate 8effe5eb4947ba88`; Sections 7--8 below record the resulting response.

The ordinary projective-energy theorem, fixed-base minimal-bad compactness, all-status cap response, and normal-dependent physical cone are the previously proved inputs. The conclusions below do not include a numerical Gamma payment.

## 1. Definition and the necessary invariant normalization

Let d>=1, N=d+1, and let P be a fixed finite complete lattice base. Let K_z be positive compatible convex d-dimensional fibers and C their canonical hull. Put

    V_z=|K_z|, M=sum_z V_z,
    E_z(y)=min_a integral_(K_z)[1+a dot(X-y)]^(-N)dX,
    F(z,y)=E_z(y)^(1/d), v(z)=|C_z|^(1/d).

As usual extend E, hence F, by zero at own-fiber boundary marks. Define

    H(z,y)=[E_z(y)V_z^(1/d)]^(1/N),
    f_H(z,y)=H(z,y)/M^(1/d).                              (1)

On real fibers use the actual v(z), so H=F^(d/N)v^(1/N). Joint energy-root concavity, Brunn--Minkowski, and concavity of the positive weighted geometric mean make H concave on C. On each positive fiber it is strictly concave in its interior, because F is strictly concave there and v is a positive constant. It is continuous up to the sampled boundaries and vanishes there. Since E_z(y)<=V_z,

    0<=f_H(z,y)<= (V_z/M)^(1/d)<=1.                       (2)

Let Sigma be the pooled within-fiber covariance normalized by M, and Gamma(u)=sqrt(u^T Sigma u). The buffered through-mark caps are

    a dot(Z-p)+u dot(X-y)>=-epsilon f_H(p,y)Gamma(u),       (3)

for arbitrary base a and nonzero continuous u, together with closed pure-base caps. Their infimum is the raw buffered depth b^H_epsilon; divide its maximum by M to obtain beta^H_epsilon.

The normalization M^(-1/d) in (1) matters. In the notation of the old formal expression (L E/M)^(1/N), it corresponds to the TIED function L_z=(V_z/M)^(1/d), not to unnormalized L_z=V_z^(1/d). Under a common continuous affine map with determinant J, E and V multiply by |J|, H multiplies by |J|^(1/d), and M^(1/d) does too. Thus f_H is invariant, while Gamma transforms covariantly with the normal. Affine continuous base shears and unimodular base changes preserve the same caps and normalized masses.

## 2. Actual attainment in the compact minimal-bad-base framework

Use exactly the ORIGINAL-depth hypotheses and compact normalization of `candidate f7c05b2c30c8cfcb`, Sections 1--2: a fixed minimal bad complete base, beta_*<b<Gamma_d/k(P), and a compact representative class A of all original sublevel families beta_0<=b with

    M=1, V_z>=v0>0, K_z subset R Ball,
    lambda_- I<=Sigma<=lambda_+ I.

No additional buffered restriction inequality is used. Every member has a common positive fiber inradius after the already proved compact positive-body argument.

The same all-normal continuity proof as in that source applies directly to (1). Fiber volumes, total mass, covariance and the energy are continuous under simultaneous positive-body Hausdorff convergence, including moving boundary marks. Therefore f_H is jointly continuous. For aligned marks in one fixed base, the cap-threshold difference for Euclidean unit continuous normal is bounded by the mark displacement plus the supremum difference of epsilon f_H Gamma. The bound is independent of the base tilt. Total symmetric-difference volume and the uniform slab bound control every cap mass; pure-base caps use the same finite subset of fibers. Infima over all caps and maxima over compact sampled fibers consequently commute with this limit by the uniform estimates.

Let A_sec=|P| omega_(d-1) R^(d-1), omega_0=1. On A, (2) gives

    0<=beta^H_epsilon(K)-beta_0(K)
         <=A_sec sqrt(lambda_+) epsilon=:C epsilon.      (4)

Choose a reference strict bad family and sufficiently small epsilon_bar so its buffered value remains below b. A minimizing sequence for beta^H_epsilon then has beta_0<=beta^H_epsilon<b. The common invariant normalizations place it in compact A, and continuity gives an actual positive minimizer. Since the infimum was over ALL positive compatible families before normalization, this is an unrestricted body minimum, not a minimum imposed by an artificial bounding ball.

## 3. Uniform source cores, floors, and a direct linear value gap

Some fiber in M=1 has volume at least 1/|P|. Its centroid gives ordinary depth at least

    q0=Gamma_d/|P|>0.

Ordinary depth is A_sec-Lipschitz in the own continuous mark and zero at the own boundary: a supporting continuous normal extends by the finite support-height LP to an ambient support cap with zero mixed d-volume. Thus every ordinary deepest mark has distance at least q0/A_sec from its own boundary.

At every buffered deepest mark, (4) instead gives distance at least (q0-C epsilon)/A_sec. Decrease epsilon_bar until C epsilon_bar<=q0/4. Then every such mark has a fixed own ball, for example radius r_s=q0/(2A_sec). The buffer displacement is at most epsilon sqrt(lambda_+); decreasing epsilon_bar again makes every nonvertical own buffered trace proper with a uniform positive coarea lower bound.

At any mark with that source ball,

    E_z(y)>=omega_d r_s^d=:E_min,
    f_H(z,y)>= [E_min v0^(1/d)]^(1/N)=:h_min>0           (5)

in the M=1 normalization. The first inequality is energy monotonicity under inclusion of the centered ball. No parameter normalization or parameter transport is used.

There is a particularly simple uniform LOWER value gap. Choose an ORDINARY deepest mark. Its source ball is uniform independently of epsilon, so (5) holds there. Every nonvertical buffered cap contains a uniform own-ball strip of width at least epsilon h_min sqrt(lambda_-), once epsilon is small. The strip has area at least omega_(d-1)(sqrt(3)r_s/2)^(d-1). Thus its captured mass exceeds the corresponding ordinary cap by at least c1 epsilon. Pure-base caps have the exact own-fiber reserve

    baseDepth(p)-ordinaryDepth(p,y)>=V_p/2>=v0/2,

from the opposite-continuous-perturbation lemma. For epsilon<=v0/(2c1), taking the infimum over BOTH cap types gives

    beta^H_epsilon(K)>=beta_0(K)+c1 epsilon             (6)

uniformly over A. There is no need for deepest-face exhaustion here: (5) holds at every ordinary deepest mark. Combining (4)--(6) gives

    beta_*+c1 epsilon <= inf_K beta^H_epsilon(K)
                       <=beta_*+C epsilon              (7)

for sufficiently small epsilon; competitors outside the original sublevel cannot improve the right-hand trial bound.

The same reserve and (4) also give, at every buffered deepest base,

    baseDepth(p)-Q_epsilon>=V_p/2-C epsilon>=v0/4.       (8)

Hence the small-epsilon problem has no atomic deepest groups.

## 4. Optional actual logarithmic scale selection

For tau>0 minimize beta^H_epsilon(K)-tau log epsilon over 0<epsilon<=epsilon_bar and all positive compatible bodies. A trial epsilon=tau/C has objective tending to beta_*<b. At fixed tau the penalty prevents epsilon from tending to zero; the body-only compactness and joint continuity prove attainment. The two-sided estimate (7) gives epsilon_tau comparable to tau by the elementary scalar comparison used in the archived scale-selection theorem. In particular epsilon_tau is interior for small tau.

Every such minimizer is an actual body minimum at its fixed epsilon. Both signs of dot(log epsilon) are feasible. If the actual common separator below is constructed for the stated response cone with this extra scalar direction, its unchanged scalar coefficient is

    Delta=M tau.                                        (9)

Alternatively one may work only with the attained fixed-epsilon problems; none of the first-response formulas below requires scale selection.

## 5. Exact source charts, with a uniform global floor

Let a_Y be the attained projective normalizer at an interior source Y=(p,y):

    P_Y(X)=1+a_Y dot(X-y).

The known interior derivative is grad_y log E=N a_Y. Since V_p does not depend on the continuous mark,

    grad_y log f_H=grad_y log H=a_Y.                     (10)

This is the desired exact alignment.

Choose full affine majorants S>=F and T>=v touching at Y and p, respectively. Their existence at boundary bases and bounded choices on a uniform source-interior class are supplied by the actual energy-supergradient and finite-hull support arguments. Define

    R_Y=(d/N) S/F(Y)+(1/N) T/v(p).                      (11)

Weighted AM--GM gives H(Y)R_Y>=H globally; equality holds at Y. Its continuous slope is a_Y, so its own-fiber restriction is EXACTLY P_Y. Furthermore S>=0 and T>=v_min imply

    R_Y>=v_min/[N v(p)]>=v_min/(N v_max)>0.             (12)

With common inner/outer radii r,R, this is at least r/(N R). Thus these are globally positive, uniformly controlled chart denominators, without any vanishing PL multiplier. Independently, the ordinary tangent inequality for F on the own fiber gives S/F(Y)=1+(N/d)a_Y dot(X-y)>=0 and hence P_Y>=1/N there.

On a maximal occupied deepest-source face, equality of H at anchored deepest interpolations forces equality in F and v and constant F/v. Marked-energy equality then supplies the exact homothetic source family. Choosing S and T at its relative-interior integer witness q makes H(Y_q)R_q touch H at all of that face's sources. The individually normalized chart there is R_q/R_q(Y_i), not an assertion that R_q equals one at every source. This is the body-tied version of the coherent chart construction; it does not use or create parameter rows.

## 6. Exact signed first response

Take an ACTUAL compatible signed body path with inward normal speed v_z(X). Define

    D_z=integral_(partial K_z) v_z dS,    D=sum_z D_z,
    C_E,Y=integral_(partial K_p) P_Y^(-N) v_p dS.

The signed energy envelope at a fixed old interior mark gives dot E=-C_E,Y. Also dot V_z=-D_z and dot M=-D. Therefore (1) yields

    dot f_H/f_H = -C_E,Y/(N E_Y)
                   -D_p/(d N V_p)+D/(d M).            (13)

This is an exact tied-body derivative. Substituting a body-dependent L into an old free-L response without its derivative would omit the middle term and give the wrong global mass coefficient.

For Gamma(u)=1 define

    J(u)=sum_z integral_(partial K_z)
                    [u dot(X-g_z)]^2 v_z dS.

The pooled covariance derivative gives dot Gamma/Gamma=D/(2M)-J(u)/(2M). Centroid derivatives disappear against the old centered first moments. Thus a contact with scalar buffer delta=epsilon f_H has fractional full-buffer response

    -C_E,Y/(N E_Y)-D_p/(d N V_p)
             +(d+2)D/(2d M)-J(u)/(2M).                (14)

For a group i with fixed old probability weights rho_ij, Gamma(u_ij)=1, normal velocities nu_ij, and a finite old contact Y_ia, let J_i=sum_j rho_ij J(u_ij). Its actual affine-minus-buffer contact-budget coefficient is

    sum_j rho_ij nu_ij dot Y_ia
      -delta_ia sum_j rho_ij grad Gamma(u_ij) dot dot u_ij
      +delta_ia[ C_E,ia/(N E_ia)+D_(p_ia)/(d N V_(p_ia))
                   +J_i/(2M)-(d+2)D/(2dM)-s ],        (15)

where s=dot(log epsilon), omitted for fixed scale. The group budget takes the minimum over its actual old contacts. The signed energy envelope makes this expansion uniform near their finite source cores, exactly as in the established finite-contact continuation. The continuous contact relation is now

    U_i=sum_j rho_ij u_ij=delta_ia a_ia                 (16)

at every positively used contact.

## 7. The SAME-separator density

The companion `candidate 8effe5eb4947ba88` constructs the actual finite cover, all-status cap continuation, and simultaneous convex physical-field realization for this NEW H problem, using (15). Retain the common cap/contact/outside-selector coefficients constructed there. Let kappa_ia be the contact force coefficients,

    e_ia=kappa_ia delta_ia, e_i=sum_a e_ia, Delta=sum_i e_i.

Let W be the ACTUAL boundary capture selector of that same separator, including its supporting allocations. Inward body response then gives

    integral Xi_z(X) Phi(n_z(X),z,X)dS <=0             (17)

for every actually realized continuous normal-dependent globally convex physical field, where

    Xi_z(X)=W_z(X)-beta
       +sum_(ia:p_ia=z) e_ia[ P_ia(X)^(-N)/(N E_ia)
                                      +1/(d N V_z)]
       +(1/(2M))sum_i e_i sum_j rho_ij
                                 [u_ij dot(X-g_z)]^2
       -(d+2)Delta/(2d M).                             (18)

The coarea normalization and shared cap-normal equations remain the actual ones: section means use kappa-weighted source barycenters and the covariance buffer shift. Formula (16) has NO extra parameter-gradient term. There are NO parameter tests in this problem and therefore NO inherited volume martingale.

This is the H-specific separator from the companion proof. It does not reuse the old free-L separator, whose optimizing bodies and source coefficients may differ.

## 8. The attainable positive SURFACE transport law

Let sigma be ordinary boundary area on the normal bundle of all sampled fibers. Define the positive measure A by the density

    W + sum_(ia:p_ia=z)e_ia[P_ia^(-N)/(N E_ia)+1/(d N V_z)]
      +(1/(2M))sum_i e_i sum_j rho_ij[u_ij dot(X-g_z)]^2,

and put B_star=beta+(d+2)Delta/(2dM). Then (17) is exactly

    integral Phi dA <= integral Phi d(B_star sigma).     (19)

Normal-dependent affine fields and their negatives give equality of normal marginals and of full conditional physical first moments. The existing normal-preserving convex-order/martingale theorem therefore yields a normal-preserving martingale from A to B_star sigma. Its starting points are ACTUAL boundary points; its positive source/kernel/covariance/cap contributions may be retained as marks. It is not a martingale from the discrete deepest marks, and (19) does not turn source-weighted own-fiber costs into original mixed-volume allocations.

All reciprocal powers in (18) have uniform denominator floors by (12), the energies have the source-core lower bound, and V_z has a positive floor. Proper coareas bound sum kappa between fixed positive constants; (2), (5) give Delta comparable to epsilon. Thus the extra response densities are uniformly O(epsilon), with uniformly bounded coefficients after division by epsilon. W lies in [0,1]. Within this first-response package there is consequently NO inverse-parameter/logarithmic concentration branch. Actual supporting-cap boundary allocations still have to be retained, and the missing outside-cost comparison has not disappeared merely because the response is compact.
